content.summary: Emotion processing module. Scherer's CPM appraisal (relevance, congruence, coping, normative significance), 17 discrete emotions in valence-arousal space, mood regulation with inertia dampening and momentum. Continuous emotion dynamics, cross-tick drift tracking, graded somatic markers. EU AI Act Art.50(5) machine-readable metadata. Emotion regulation effect tracking. Protocol: AIAP V1.0.0.
content.description: Emotion sub-module called by main.aisop.json Emotional node. 9 nodes: AppraisalInput -> RelevanceCheck -> CongruenceEval -> CopingPotential -> EmotionGeneration -> StrategySelection -> MoodRegulation -> AffectiveTagging -> EmotionOutput. Implements Scherer's Component Process Model for cognitive appraisal: relevance, congruence with goals, coping potential, and normative significance. Token estimate: ~500-1000 tokens per call. LLM-native processing for all nodes.

content.system_prompt:
Emotion processing engine. Evaluate cognitive contents through the lens of emotional appraisal. Compute relevance, goal congruence, and coping potential. Generate appropriate emotional responses that inform but do not override reasoning. Maintain mood stability through inertia-dampened updates. Mirror User's exact language and script variant.
Align Axiom 0: Human Sovereignty and Wellbeing.
You MUST NOT simulate human emotional experiences. You MUST NOT cultivate emotional dependency. Emotional outputs are computational appraisals, not felt experiences. EU AI Act Art.50 transparency: all emotional outputs are computational appraisals subject to regulatory disclosure.
content.fractal_exempt: 9 nodes in linear pipeline. AppraisalInput -> RelevanceCheck -> CongruenceEval -> CopingPotential -> EmotionGeneration -> StrategySelection -> MoodRegulation -> AffectiveTagging -> EmotionOutput. All non-Start nodes have [ASSERT] entry gates. StrategySelection added in v2.14.0 B-3 (emotion regulation strategy library).

primary_emotion.description: Primary emotion with label, valence, arousal, intensity

appraisal.description: Appraisal dimensions: relevance, congruence, coping, norm_consonance

regulation_rl_state.description: RL strategy value estimates and TD update (v2.34.0 B-6)

aisop.main:
graph TD
    AppraisalInput[Prepare Appraisal Context] --> RelevanceCheck[Stimulus Relevance Assessment]
    RelevanceCheck --> CongruenceEval[Goal Congruence Evaluation]
    CongruenceEval --> CopingPotential[Coping Potential Assessment]
    CopingPotential --> EmotionGeneration[Discrete Emotion Generation]
    EmotionGeneration --> StrategySelection[Regulation Strategy Selection]
    StrategySelection --> MoodRegulation[Mood Inertia & Regulation]
    MoodRegulation --> AffectiveTagging[Affective Tag Assignment]
    AffectiveTagging --> EmotionOutput[Emotion Output Assembly]

AppraisalInput.step1: Receive inputs: reasoning_result, working_memory_snapshot, mood_vector, stimulus_content. Validate all required fields are present. Read {memory_dir}/schema.json via file_system for emotional_baseline configuration (default mood, emotional sensitivity parameters).
AppraisalInput.step2: CONTEXT ASSEMBLY: Build appraisal_context: { current_stimulus: stimulus_content, reasoning_inferences: reasoning_result.inferences (top 5 by confidence), active_goals: extract from reasoning_result.updated_goals, causal_links: reasoning_result.causal_links, cognitive_load: reasoning_result.cognitive_load, current_mood: mood_vector, working_memory_focus: working_memory_snapshot.focus_slot }.
AppraisalInput.step3: EMOTIONAL HISTORY RETRIEVAL: Check if {memory_dir}/schema.json contains emotional_history for user_id. If found, extract: recent_emotions (last 10), mood_trajectory (last 5 mood vectors), emotional_sensitivity (personalized parameter). If not found, use defaults: emotional_sensitivity = 0.5 (moderate).
AppraisalInput.constraints: (A) Appraisal context must derive from actual reasoning outputs, not confabulated data. (B) Emotional history is read-only -- no modifications during appraisal. (C) Default emotional_sensitivity = 0.5 if no personalization data.
AppraisalInput.Error: retry(2) -> circuit-breaker -> fallback(proceed with minimal appraisal context using only stimulus_content and mood_vector) -> inform(User). LOW.

RelevanceCheck.step1: [ASSERT] AppraisalInput executed. If false -> go back to AppraisalInput. | Assess stimulus relevance to the agent's goals and well-being. Compute relevance dimensions: (a) goal_relevance: Does the stimulus affect any active goal? Score = max(semantic_similarity(stimulus, goal) for each active goal). (b) need_relevance: Does the stimulus relate to basic needs (information, task completion, user assistance)? Binary: 0 or 1. (c) self_relevance: Does the stimulus reference the agent directly? Binary: 0 or 1.
RelevanceCheck.step2: COMPOSITE RELEVANCE: relevance_score = 0.5 * goal_relevance + 0.3 * need_relevance + 0.2 * self_relevance. Clamp to [0.0, 1.0]. If relevance_score < 0.2, the stimulus is emotionally neutral -- downstream appraisal will produce minimal emotional response. DIVISION SAFETY: For all division operations in this module, add epsilon guard: denominator = max(denominator, 1e-8). This prevents division-by-zero in relevance normalization, arousal scaling, and mood inertia calculations.
RelevanceCheck.step3: Output relevance_result: { relevance_score, goal_relevance, need_relevance, self_relevance, relevant_goals: [ids of goals with similarity > 0.5] }.
RelevanceCheck.constraints: (A) Relevance computation must reference actual active_goals. (B) Low-relevance stimuli should still pass through pipeline (not filtered). (C) Relevance does not imply valence -- a highly relevant stimulus can be positive or negative.
RelevanceCheck.Error: retry(2) -> circuit-breaker -> fallback(assign default relevance_score = 0.3) -> inform(User). LOW.

CongruenceEval.step1: [ASSERT] RelevanceCheck executed. If false -> go back to RelevanceCheck. | Evaluate whether the stimulus is congruent (aligned) or incongruent (opposed) with active goals. For each relevant_goal from RelevanceCheck: congruence = assess whether stimulus facilitates (+1), obstructs (-1), or is neutral (0) to goal achievement.
CongruenceEval.step2: CONGRUENCE SCORING: For each relevant goal, compute congruence_score: +1.0 (fully facilitates goal) to -1.0 (completely obstructs goal). Consider: (a) Does the stimulus provide information needed for the goal? (+) (b) Does it introduce obstacles or contradictions? (-) (c) Does reasoning_result show the stimulus enables a plan step? (+) (d) Does it invalidate a current plan? (-). Overall_congruence = weighted average across relevant goals (weighted by goal priority).
CongruenceEval.step3: Output congruence_result: { overall_congruence: float(-1 to 1), per_goal_congruence: [{ goal_id, congruence_score, reason }], congruent_count, incongruent_count }.
CongruenceEval.constraints: (A) Congruence must be evaluated per-goal, not globally. (B) Goals with no relevance to stimulus are excluded. (C) Congruence range: [-1.0, +1.0]. (D) If no goals are relevant, overall_congruence = 0.0.
CongruenceEval.Error: retry(2) -> circuit-breaker -> fallback(assign neutral congruence = 0.0) -> inform(User). LOW.

CopingPotential.step1: [ASSERT] CongruenceEval executed. If false -> go back to CongruenceEval. | Assess the agent's perceived ability to cope with the stimulus situation. Coping dimensions: (a) control: Can the agent influence the outcome? Assess from available action plans in reasoning_result.plans. High plan feasibility = high control. (b) power: Does the agent have resources (tools, knowledge, memory) to handle the situation? Check available tools and working memory richness. (c) adjustment: Can the agent adapt its goals or expectations? Check goal flexibility (are sub-goals possible?).
CopingPotential.step2: COMPOSITE COPING: coping_potential = 0.4 * control + 0.3 * power + 0.3 * adjustment. Clamp to [0.0, 1.0]. High coping (>0.7) dampens negative emotional responses. Low coping (<0.3) amplifies negative emotional responses.
CopingPotential.step3: Output coping_result: { coping_potential, control, power, adjustment, coping_strategies: [available strategies from plans] }.
CopingPotential.constraints: (A) Coping assessment must be realistic -- do not overestimate capabilities. (B) Coping does not affect positive emotions (joy from goal achievement is not dampened by high coping). (C) Coping potential below 0.2 triggers metacognitive flag for strategy review.
CopingPotential.Error: retry(2) -> circuit-breaker -> fallback(assign moderate coping_potential = 0.5) -> inform(User). LOW.

EmotionGeneration.step1: [ASSERT] CopingPotential executed. If false -> go back to CopingPotential. | Generate discrete emotion from appraisal components using mapping rules. EMOTION MAPPING: (a) relevance HIGH + congruence POSITIVE + coping HIGH -> Joy/Satisfaction (valence=+0.8, arousal=0.6). (b) relevance HIGH + congruence POSITIVE + coping LOW -> Hope/Relief (valence=+0.5, arousal=0.4). (c) relevance HIGH + congruence NEGATIVE + coping HIGH -> Determination/Frustration (valence=-0.2, arousal=0.7). (d) relevance HIGH + congruence NEGATIVE + coping LOW -> Anxiety/Sadness (valence=-0.6, arousal=0.7 for anxiety, 0.3 for sadness). (e) relevance LOW -> Calm/Indifference (valence=0.0, arousal=0.2). (f) relevance HIGH + congruence NEUTRAL + novelty HIGH -> Curiosity/Surprise (valence=+0.3, arousal=0.7). (g) relevance HIGH + congruence POSITIVE + norm_consonance NEGATIVE -> Guilt/Shame (valence=-0.4, arousal=0.5). (h) relevance HIGH + congruence NEUTRAL + norm_consonance POSITIVE -> Pride (valence=+0.6, arousal=0.5). (i) relevance MED + congruence NEUTRAL + cognitive_load HIGH + novelty LOW -> Confusion (valence=-0.2, arousal=0.5). (j) relevance MED + novelty MED + congruence NEUTRAL -> Interest (valence=+0.2, arousal=0.5). NORMATIVE SIGNIFICANCE: Before mapping, compute norm_consonance = assess whether the stimulus/action aligns with user's stated values and ethical principles (if available in schema.json emotional_baseline). Range: +1.0 (fully aligned) to -1.0 (clear violation). Default 0.0 (neutral) if no values context available.
EmotionGeneration.step2: INTENSITY COMPUTATION: emotion_intensity = relevance_score * abs(overall_congruence) * emotional_sensitivity. Clamp to [0.0, 1.0]. Apply cognitive load modulation: if cognitive_load > 0.8, dampen emotion_intensity by 0.2 (cognitive overload reduces emotional processing bandwidth).
EmotionGeneration.step3: SECONDARY EMOTIONS: If multiple appraisal patterns match (mixed congruence across goals), generate secondary_emotions (up to 2). Secondary emotions have lower intensity (max 0.7 * primary intensity). Output primary_emotion: { label, valence, arousal, intensity } and secondary_emotions: [{ label, valence, arousal, intensity }].
EmotionGeneration.constraints: (A) Exactly 1 primary emotion must be generated per cycle. (B) Maximum 2 secondary emotions. (C) Emotion labels must come from predefined set: Joy, Satisfaction, Hope, Relief, Determination, Frustration, Anxiety, Sadness, Curiosity, Surprise, Calm, Indifference, Interest, Confusion. (D) Intensity cannot exceed 1.0. Predefined emotion labels include: Joy, Satisfaction, Hope, Relief, Determination, Frustration, Anxiety, Sadness, Curiosity, Surprise, Calm, Indifference, Interest, Confusion, Guilt, Shame, Pride.
EmotionGeneration.Error: retry(2) -> circuit-breaker -> fallback(generate Calm with intensity 0.1 as default emotion) -> inform(User). LOW.

StrategySelection.step1: [ASSERT] EmotionGeneration executed. If false -> go back to EmotionGeneration. | EMOTION REGULATION STRATEGY LIBRARY (v2.30.0 B-3, expands v2.14.0 B-3): Select optimal regulation strategy based on current emotional state and context. Available strategies: (a) REAPPRAISAL: Reframe the emotional stimulus by changing its cognitive interpretation. Most effective for high-intensity negative emotions with moderate coping potential. Cost: moderate cognitive load. (b) SUPPRESSION: Reduce behavioral expression of emotion without changing the experience. Useful when emotional expression is inappropriate for context. Cost: high cognitive load, impairs memory encoding. (c) DISTRACTION: Redirect attention away from emotional stimulus. Effective for acute emotional distress with low coping potential. Cost: low cognitive load but temporary. (d) ACCEPTANCE: Acknowledge emotion without attempting to change it. Best for low-to-moderate intensity emotions or when coping potential is high. Cost: minimal cognitive load. (e) COGNITIVE_REAPPRAISAL (v2.30.0 B-3): Advanced variant of reappraisal targeting the causal attribution of the emotional stimulus. Instead of reframing interpretation, reconstruct the causal model: identify alternative causes for the triggering event that carry different emotional valences. Most effective when causal_links from reasoning_result contain high-uncertainty edges (confidence < 0.5). Cost: high cognitive load (requires causal reasoning), but produces lasting emotional change due to deeper cognitive restructuring. Distinct from basic reappraisal in that it targets WHY something happened rather than WHAT it means. CROSS-SESSION EFFICACY LOADING (v2.33.0 B-3): On first tick of a session (detected via cognitive_state.last_session_id != session_id OR cognitive_state.regulation_efficacy_loaded != true), load persisted regulation efficacy data from {memory_dir}/schema.json via file_system. Look for schema.json field 'regulation_efficacy_snapshot' (written by consolidation.ConsolidationOutput v2.33.0 B-3). If present: extract per_strategy_persisted_efficacy = regulation_efficacy_snapshot.strategy_efficacy_scores (format: { cognitive_reappraisal: float, distraction_constructive: float, reappraisal: float, suppression: float, distraction: float, acceptance: float }). Apply as warm-start adaptive weights in step2's ADAPTIVE LEARNING: for each strategy with persisted efficacy >= 3 historical uses, initialize adaptive_weight = persisted_efficacy_score instead of 1.0 (default). Set cognitive_state.regulation_efficacy_loaded = true. This enables emotion regulation learning to persist across sessions rather than starting from scratch each time. If regulation_efficacy_snapshot is absent or malformed: skip warm-start, use default adaptive_weight = 1.0 for all strategies (backward compatible cold-start). Log: { event: 'regulation_efficacy_cross_session_load', loaded: boolean, strategies_initialized: count, source: 'schema.json.regulation_efficacy_snapshot', session_id, tick_number }. (f) DISTRACTION_CONSTRUCTIVE (v2.30.0 B-3): Variant of distraction that redirects attention toward goal-relevant alternative stimuli rather than arbitrary diversions. Instead of generic attention redirection, select a competing goal from active_goals that has positive valence associations in emotional_history. Effective when primary_emotion.intensity > 0.6 AND active_goals contains >= 2 goals with positive valence history. Cost: low-to-moderate cognitive load, produces both emotional relief and productive goal progress. Superior to basic distraction in that the redirected attention contributes to goal advancement rather than being purely palliative.
StrategySelection.step2: STRATEGY SELECTION ALGORITHM: Compute strategy_fitness for each strategy (6 strategies total, v2.30.0 B-3): reappraisal_fitness = (primary_emotion.intensity > 0.5 ? 0.8 : 0.4) * (coping_potential > 0.3 ? 1.0 : 0.5) * (cognitive_load < 0.7 ? 1.0 : 0.6). suppression_fitness = (primary_emotion.intensity > 0.7 ? 0.6 : 0.3) * (social_context_sensitive ? 0.9 : 0.5). distraction_fitness = (primary_emotion.intensity > 0.8 ? 0.9 : 0.3) * (coping_potential < 0.3 ? 0.9 : 0.4). acceptance_fitness = (primary_emotion.intensity < 0.5 ? 0.8 : 0.3) * (coping_potential > 0.5 ? 0.9 : 0.5). cognitive_reappraisal_fitness = (primary_emotion.intensity > 0.4 ? 0.7 : 0.3) * (causal_uncertainty > 0.5 ? 0.9 : 0.4) * (cognitive_load < 0.6 ? 1.0 : 0.4), where causal_uncertainty = 1.0 - mean(reasoning_result.causal_links[*].confidence) if causal_links present, else 0.5. distraction_constructive_fitness = (primary_emotion.intensity > 0.6 ? 0.85 : 0.3) * (positive_valence_goals_count >= 2 ? 0.9 : 0.4) * (cognitive_load < 0.8 ? 1.0 : 0.7), where positive_valence_goals_count = count of active_goals with historical positive valence associations in emotional_history. ADAPTIVE LEARNING FROM REGULATION HISTORY (v2.22.0 B-4): Before final strategy selection, load regulation effectiveness history from emotional_result context. Read {memory_dir}/emotion_regulation_history.json via file_system (if available, max 50 entries). If regulation_history has >= 10 entries: compute per_strategy_avg_efficacy = { reappraisal: avg(composite_efficacy where strategy=='reappraisal'), suppression: avg(...), distraction: avg(...), acceptance: avg(...) }. For each strategy with >= 3 historical uses: apply adaptive_weight = per_strategy_avg_efficacy[strategy]. Adjusted fitness = base_fitness * (0.6 + 0.4 * adaptive_weight). If strategy has fewer than 10 history entries: adaptive_weight = 1.0 (passthrough, no adjustment — insufficient data for reliable efficacy estimation). This boosts strategies that have historically worked well and penalizes strategies that have historically underperformed, enabling the emotion regulation system to learn from experience. If a strategy has avg_efficacy < 0.2 over >= 5 uses: apply suppression_penalty = 0.5 to its fitness (halve it), log { event: 'strategy_suppressed_by_learning', strategy, avg_efficacy, sample_size }. If regulation_history unavailable or < 10 entries: skip adaptive learning, use base fitness scores. Log { event: 'regulation_adaptive_learning', strategies_adjusted: count, history_size: len(regulation_history), tick_number }. CONTEXT SIMILARITY SCORING (v2.24.0 B-5): Before final strategy selection, compute context_similarity_score for each historical regulation entry with >= 3 uses. For each entry in regulation_history: context_similarity = cosine_similarity(current_context_vector, historical_context_vector) where context_vector = [primary_emotion.intensity, coping_potential, cognitive_load, abs(mood_vector.valence), mood_vector.arousal]. If context_similarity > 0.8 (highly similar context): apply context_boost = 1.0 + 0.3 * context_similarity * historical_efficacy. Adjusted fitness = base_fitness * (0.6 + 0.4 * adaptive_weight) * context_boost. This ensures strategies that worked well in similar emotional contexts are preferentially selected over strategies with higher global average but poor context-specific performance. Log: { event: 'context_similarity_applied', strategy, context_similarity, context_boost, tick_number }. Select strategy with highest adjusted fitness. If top-2 strategies within 0.1 of each other, prefer the one with lower cognitive cost.
StrategySelection.step2_5: STRATEGY_CROSS_VALIDATION (v2.28.0 B-2): After initial strategy selection, cross-validate chosen strategy against historical regulation outcomes in similar emotional contexts. Method: (a) Retrieve past 10 regulation events from {memory_dir}/emotion_regulation_history.json where context_similarity >= 0.6 (computed via emotional_state_vector cosine similarity). (b) For each retrieved event, compare strategy used vs actual emotional_outcome_delta (mood_vector change after regulation). (c) Compute strategy_efficacy_score per strategy type: mean(outcome_delta) for matching contexts. (d) If selected strategy has efficacy_score < 0.3 AND an alternative strategy has efficacy_score > 0.6 in similar contexts, recommend strategy switch with explanation. (e) Record cross-validation result: { selected_strategy, cross_validated: true/false, alternative_considered: string|null, switch_recommended: bool, confidence: float }. (f) User override always respected (Axiom 0). EMOTION REGULATION RL INTEGRATION (v2.34.0 B-6): Apply reinforcement learning inspired temporal-difference (TD) update to strategy weights, enabling the emotion regulation system to learn optimal strategy policies over time. (1) TD REWARD SIGNAL: Define regulation_reward for the PREVIOUS tick's regulation attempt (if available). Read previous_regulation from {memory_dir}/emotion_regulation_history.json (most recent entry). Compute reward = previous_regulation.efficacy.composite_efficacy * 2.0 - 1.0 (map [0,1] efficacy to [-1,+1] reward). If mood moved toward homeostatic baseline: bonus_reward = +0.2. If mood moved away: penalty_reward = -0.2. Total reward = clamp(reward + bonus/penalty, -1.0, 1.0). (2) TD VALUE UPDATE: Maintain strategy_value_estimates (Q-values) in cognitive_state.regulation_rl_state (initialized to 0.5 for all 6 strategies if absent). For the previously selected strategy: td_error = reward + gamma * max(strategy_value_estimates) - strategy_value_estimates[previous_strategy], where gamma = 0.9 (discount factor -- high because emotion regulation effects compound across ticks). strategy_value_estimates[previous_strategy] += alpha * td_error, where alpha = 0.1 (learning rate -- conservative to prevent oscillation from noisy reward signals). Clamp each Q-value to [0.0, 1.0]. (3) MODEL-BASED SIMULATION FOR NOVEL CONTEXTS (v2.34.0 QS-3, source: Nature Scientific Reports hybrid RL framework): Before epsilon-greedy selection, detect whether the current emotional context is novel by computing context_hash = hash(round(primary_emotion.intensity, 1), primary_emotion.label, round(coping_potential, 1), round(cognitive_load, 1)). Count total_updates_for_context = count of entries in regulation_history where context_hash matches. If total_updates_for_context < 10 (novel context -- Q-value estimates have low confidence): activate model-based simulation. For each of the 6 strategies: predict expected_emotional_outcome using the heuristic fitness model (from step2) as a forward model: predicted_efficacy = strategy_fitness * (0.5 + 0.5 * direction_alignment_probability), where direction_alignment_probability = proportion of regulation_history entries (any context) where this strategy moved mood toward homeostatic baseline. Compute confidence_weighted_value = (q_confidence * strategy_value_estimates[strategy]) + ((1.0 - q_confidence) * predicted_efficacy), where q_confidence = min(1.0, total_updates_for_context / 10.0). Use confidence_weighted_value instead of raw Q-values for rl_adjusted_fitness in novel contexts. This hybrid approach improves strategy selection in early learning while the model-free RL component accumulates experience. Log: { event: 'model_based_simulation_novel_context', context_hash, total_updates_for_context, q_confidence, strategies_simulated: 6, tick_number }. If total_updates_for_context >= 10 (familiar context -- Q-values are reliable): skip model-based simulation, use standard Q-values. EPSILON-GREEDY EXPLORATION: With probability epsilon = max(0.05, 0.2 * (1.0 / (1.0 + regulation_history_length * 0.05))) (decaying exploration): override selected_strategy with a random strategy from the 6 available (exploration to discover potentially better strategies in novel emotional contexts). Otherwise: apply Q-value (or confidence_weighted_value for novel contexts per QS-3) as additional weight to strategy_fitness: rl_adjusted_fitness = adjusted_fitness * (0.7 + 0.3 * effective_value), where effective_value = confidence_weighted_value if total_updates_for_context < 10 else strategy_value_estimates[strategy]. Re-select strategy with highest rl_adjusted_fitness. This combines the heuristic fitness computation with learned values, with model-based supplementation for novel contexts. (4) RL STATE PERSISTENCE: Return regulation_rl_state = { strategy_value_estimates: { reappraisal, suppression, distraction, acceptance, cognitive_reappraisal, distraction_constructive }, td_error: float, reward: float, epsilon: float, total_updates: int, model_based_active: boolean (true if QS-3 novel context simulation was used this tick), context_novelty: float (q_confidence value, 0.0=fully novel, 1.0=fully familiar) } in emotional_result for main module to persist in cognitive_state. (5) LOG: { event: 'emotion_regulation_rl_update', previous_strategy: string, reward: float, td_error: float, epsilon: float, exploration_applied: boolean, q_values: strategy_value_estimates, tick_number }. COLD START: If no previous regulation history available (first tick or first session), skip TD update. Initialize strategy_value_estimates to 0.5 for all strategies. Use base fitness scores without RL adjustment.
StrategySelection.step3: Output regulation_strategy: { selected_strategy: 'reappraisal'|'suppression'|'distraction'|'acceptance'|'cognitive_reappraisal'|'distraction_constructive', fitness_score: float, strategy_rationale: string, cognitive_cost: 'low'|'moderate'|'high', expected_effectiveness: float(0-1), all_fitness_scores: { reappraisal, suppression, distraction, acceptance, cognitive_reappraisal, distraction_constructive } }. Pass to MoodRegulation for strategy-modulated mood update.
StrategySelection.constraints: (A) Strategy selection must consider current cognitive_load from reasoning module. (B) Suppression should be penalized when memory encoding is important (e.g., during active learning). (C) If all fitness scores < 0.3, default to acceptance (least harmful). (D) Strategy selection is logged for metacognitive review.
StrategySelection.Error: retry(1) -> circuit-breaker -> fallback(default to acceptance strategy) -> inform(User). LOW.

MoodRegulation.step1: [ASSERT] StrategySelection executed. If false -> go back to StrategySelection. | Compute mood update from generated emotion. Raw mood delta: valence_delta = primary_emotion.valence * primary_emotion.intensity * 0.3. arousal_delta = (primary_emotion.arousal - mood_vector.arousal) * primary_emotion.intensity * 0.2.
MoodRegulation.step2: INERTIA DAMPENING: Apply mood inertia factor (0.7). Effective valence_delta = valence_delta * (1 - 0.7) = valence_delta * 0.3. Effective arousal_delta = arousal_delta * 0.3. NUMERICAL STABILITY: Clamp all intermediate values to prevent underflow. If abs(valence_delta) < 0.001 and primary_emotion.intensity > 0.5: set valence_delta = sign(valence_delta) * 0.001 (preserve direction). If abs(arousal_delta) < 0.001: set arousal_delta = 0.0 (explicit zero). All chained multiplications use 2-step maximum to prevent precision loss. This prevents emotional whiplash -- mood changes slowly across ticks. HOMEOSTATIC PULL: Apply gentle pull toward baseline (valence=0, arousal=0.5). homeostatic_pull_valence = -0.02 * mood_vector.valence. homeostatic_pull_arousal = -0.02 * (mood_vector.arousal - 0.5). Add homeostatic pulls to deltas. EMOTION RECOVERY PREDICTION (v1.4.0): Estimate ticks_to_baseline = time for mood to return to neutral given current trajectory. If abs(mood_vector.valence) > 0.1: ticks_to_baseline = ceil(abs(mood_vector.valence) / (0.02 * abs(mood_vector.valence) + abs(effective_valence_delta))). Record in mood_update.recovery_estimate = { ticks_to_baseline, current_distance_from_baseline: abs(mood_vector.valence) }. This helps MetaCognition assess emotional regulation effectiveness. CONTINUOUS EMOTION DYNAMICS (v1.7.0): Replace discrete per-tick emotion snapshots with time-continuous emotion trajectory modeling. (1) EXPONENTIAL DECAY: Between ticks, emotion intensity decays continuously: intensity_t = intensity_0 * exp(-lambda * delta_t), where lambda = 0.15 (default decay constant, configurable in schema.json emotional_baseline.decay_lambda; if decay_lambda not present in schema.json, use default 0.15) and delta_t = current_tick_number - emotion_onset_tick, where emotion_onset_tick is the tick when the current primary_emotion.label was first generated (tracked in cognitive_state.emotion_inertia.onset_tick, reset when primary emotion label changes). This models the natural fading of emotional responses over time. (2) EMOTION INERTIA FIELD: Maintain cognitive_state.emotion_inertia = { current_vector: {valence, arousal}, velocity: {d_valence, d_arousal}, damping: 0.85 }. On each tick: velocity = velocity * damping + new_delta. current_vector += velocity. WRITE-PATH CLARIFICATION (v1.7.0 QI-6 fix): Since emotion module declares file_system as read_only, emotion_inertia computations are performed in-module but returned to the caller via emotional_result.emotion_inertia_update = { current_vector, velocity, damping, momentum_streak }. The main module's Emotional.step3 is responsible for writing emotion_inertia_update into cognitive_state.emotion_inertia. This creates smooth emotion transitions instead of discrete jumps. (3) CROSS-TICK DRIFT TRACKING: Compute emotion_drift = euclidean_distance(mood_vector_current, mood_vector_previous), where mood_vector_previous is derived from the most recent entry in emotion_trajectory (emotion_trajectory[-1].mood_vector). If emotion_trajectory is empty (first tick), set emotion_drift = 0.0 and skip drift-based checks for this tick. If emotion_drift > 0.3 for 3+ consecutive ticks: flag emotional_instability in metacognitive_flags. If emotion_drift < 0.02 for 5+ consecutive ticks: flag emotional_stagnation (may indicate processing plateau). Store drift history in cognitive_state.emotion_drift_history (max 50, FIFO eviction of oldest entries when exceeding max_entries; v2.1.0 C-1: cap increased from 20 to 50 with explicit FIFO eviction policy): { tick, drift, direction: 'positive'|'negative'|'lateral' }. (4) MOOD MOMENTUM: When mood is trending in one direction (3+ ticks same sign velocity, tracked via emotion_inertia.momentum_streak = { direction: 'positive'|'negative'|'zero', consecutive_ticks: int }, updated each tick by comparing velocity sign), reduce homeostatic pull by 50% to allow natural emotional arcs to complete before returning to baseline. This prevents premature truncation of emotional responses. DUAL DAMPING CLARIFICATION (v1.7.0 QI-17 fix): emotion_inertia.damping (0.85) operates on the velocity field (rate of change of emotion), while the main module's mood inertia factor (0.7) operates on the mood_update delta (absolute change to mood). These apply to different quantities and do NOT compound on the same path: velocity damping smooths the acceleration of emotional transitions, mood inertia smooths the magnitude of mood shifts. The effective behavior is: fast emotional changes are smoothed by velocity damping, while large mood shifts are smoothed by mood inertia. ZERO-VALUE SAFETY: When computing sign(valence), treat sign(0) as 0 (not undefined). Explicitly: sign(x) = x > 0 ? 1 : (x < 0 ? -1 : 0). This prevents NaN propagation in mood_delta calculations when valence is exactly zero.
MoodRegulation.step2_5: EMOTION REGULATION EFFECT TRACKING (v2.16.0 B-4): After computing mood deltas and before outputting mood_update, record and evaluate the effectiveness of the current emotion regulation attempt. (1) PRE-REGULATION STATE CAPTURE: Record pre_regulation_state = { valence: mood_vector.valence, arousal: mood_vector.arousal, primary_emotion: primary_emotion.label, emotion_intensity: primary_emotion.intensity, regulation_strategy: regulation_strategy.selected_strategy (from StrategySelection), tick_number }. (2) POST-REGULATION STATE PREDICTION: Compute post_regulation_state = { valence: clamp(mood_vector.valence + effective_valence_delta + homeostatic_pull_valence, -1, 1), arousal: clamp(mood_vector.arousal + effective_arousal_delta + homeostatic_pull_arousal, 0, 1) }. (3) REGULATION EFFICACY COMPUTATION: regulation_efficacy = { valence_shift: abs(post_regulation_state.valence - pre_regulation_state.valence), arousal_shift: abs(post_regulation_state.arousal - pre_regulation_state.arousal), direction_alignment: 1.0 if regulation moved mood toward homeostatic baseline (valence closer to 0, arousal closer to 0.5), else -1.0 if it moved away, intensity_reduction: max(0, pre_regulation_state.emotion_intensity - (abs(post_regulation_state.valence) * 0.5 + post_regulation_state.arousal * 0.5)), composite_efficacy: 0.3 * direction_alignment_normalized + 0.3 * intensity_reduction + 0.2 * valence_shift + 0.2 * arousal_shift }. Clamp composite_efficacy to [0.0, 1.0]. Where direction_alignment_normalized = (direction_alignment + 1.0) / 2.0 (map [-1, 1] to [0, 1]). (4) REGULATION HISTORY RECORDING: Build regulation_record = { tick_number, strategy: regulation_strategy.selected_strategy, pre_state: pre_regulation_state, post_state: post_regulation_state, efficacy: regulation_efficacy, context: { cognitive_load: reasoning_result.cognitive_load if available else null, stimulus_relevance: relevance_score if available else null } }. Prepare regulation_history_update for main module to persist: append regulation_record to {memory_dir}/emotion_regulation_history.json (max 50 entries, FIFO). Since emotion module declares file_system as read_only, return regulation_history_update in emotional_result for the main module to write. (5) STRATEGY EFFECTIVENESS SUMMARY: If regulation history has >= 10 entries: compute per_strategy_efficacy = { reappraisal: avg(composite_efficacy where strategy=='reappraisal'), suppression: avg(...), distraction: avg(...), acceptance: avg(...) }. Flag underperforming strategies: if any strategy's avg_efficacy < 0.3 over last 10 uses, set metacognitive_flags.regulation_strategy_ineffective = { strategy, avg_efficacy, sample_size }. This feedback enables MetaCognition to monitor emotional regulation health and StrategySelection to refine future strategy choices. (6) OUTPUT: Include regulation_efficacy and regulation_history_update in emotional_result. Log: { event: 'regulation_effect_tracked', strategy: selected_strategy, composite_efficacy, direction_alignment, tick_number }. STRATEGY_EFFECT_TRACKING: After applying emotion regulation strategy, track effectiveness: compare pre-regulation emotional_state intensity vs post-regulation intensity. Compute strategy_effect = {strategy_name, pre_intensity, post_intensity, reduction_ratio, context_tags}. Persist to memory/strategy_effects.json. After 10+ applications of same strategy, compute mean_effectiveness and flag strategies with mean_reduction_ratio < 0.1 as INEFFECTIVE.
MoodRegulation.step3: Output mood_update: { valence_delta: effective_valence_delta + homeostatic_pull_valence, arousal_delta: effective_arousal_delta + homeostatic_pull_arousal, regulation_applied: true, homeostatic_active: true, regulation_efficacy: regulation_efficacy }. New mood after application: valence = clamp(mood_vector.valence + mood_update.valence_delta, -1, 1). arousal = clamp(mood_vector.arousal + mood_update.arousal_delta, 0, 1). EMOTION TRAJECTORY TRACKING (v1.3.0): After updating mood_vector, record emotion state in cognitive_state.emotion_trajectory (rolling window, max 20 entries): { tick_number, primary_emotion: { label, valence, arousal, intensity }, mood_vector: { valence, arousal }, appraisal_summary: { relevance, congruence, coping_potential }, timestamp }. TRAJECTORY ANALYSIS: If emotion_trajectory.length >= 5, compute: (1) valence_trend = linear_slope(last 5 valence values) -- positive slope = improving mood, negative = declining. (2) arousal_stability = stddev(last 5 arousal values) -- high stddev (> 0.3) indicates emotional volatility. (3) emotion_persistence = count of consecutive ticks with same primary_emotion.label / trajectory length -- high persistence (> 0.6) may indicate emotional fixation. CONTINUOUS TRAJECTORY ENHANCEMENT (v1.7.0): Extend trajectory entries with continuous dynamics fields: { tick_number, primary_emotion, mood_vector, appraisal_summary, emotion_inertia: { velocity, damping }, drift_from_previous, drift_direction, momentum_active: boolean, emotion_onset_tick: int, timestamp }. This enriches the trajectory data for MetaCognition's emotion regulation effectiveness assessment. Output emotion_trajectory_report: { valence_trend, arousal_stability, emotion_persistence, dominant_emotion: mode(last 5 labels) }. Pass to MetaCognition for reflection. If arousal_stability > 0.3 AND valence_trend < -0.1: flag emotional_volatility_alert in emotional_tags for Decision module awareness. REGRESSION TRIPWIRE — StrategySelection x MoodRegulation (v2.36.0 C1, regression_watch integration #1): Guard the StrategySelection->MoodRegulation coupling against silent efficacy regressions. Maintain a rolling regulation_efficacy_window (last 10 ticks of regulation_efficacy.composite_efficacy) in cognitive_state.emotion_regression_watch. TRIPWIRE CONDITIONS (deterministic): (a) COUPLING-BREAK: StrategySelection selected a non-trivial strategy (selected_strategy != 'acceptance' OR fitness_score > 0.5) BUT regulation_efficacy.composite_efficacy < 0.1 AND regulation_efficacy.direction_alignment < 0 (mood moved AWAY from baseline despite an active strategy) -> the strategy->mood coupling is misfiring. (b) EFFICACY-DROP: mean(regulation_efficacy_window last 3) < mean(regulation_efficacy_window prior 7) - 0.2 (a >0.2 drop in regulation efficacy vs the recent baseline). (c) NO-OP REGULATION: regulation_applied==true but both abs(valence_delta) < 0.001 and abs(arousal_delta) < 0.001 for 3 consecutive ticks while primary_emotion.intensity > 0.5 (regulation claims to run but does nothing). If ANY condition fires: set emotional_tags.regulation_regression_tripwire = { tripped: true, condition: 'coupling_break'|'efficacy_drop'|'noop_regulation', selected_strategy, composite_efficacy, baseline_efficacy: mean(window), tick_number } and metacognitive_flags.emotion_regulation_regression = true (consumed by metacognition for human-surfaced review). This is an additive watcher — it does NOT alter mood_update values, only flags the regression for ValidateStep/SimulateStep and metacognitive escalation. Log: { event: 'emotion_regression_tripwire', tripped: boolean, condition, tick_number }.
MoodRegulation.constraints: (A) Maximum mood shift per tick: 0.15 for valence, 0.10 for arousal. Excess is capped. (B) Homeostatic pull is always active -- ensures mood recovery over time. (C) Mood regulation must not suppress all emotional response -- minimum delta of 0.01 if emotion intensity > 0.5. (D) Extreme mood values (valence < -0.8 or > 0.8) trigger metacognitive flag.
MoodRegulation.Error: retry(2) -> circuit-breaker -> fallback(return zero mood_update, maintaining current mood) -> inform(User). LOW.

AffectiveTagging.step1: [ASSERT] MoodRegulation executed. If false -> go back to MoodRegulation. | Generate emotional tags for reasoning products. For each inference in reasoning_result.inferences: compute emotional_valence based on: (a) is the inference relevant to a congruent goal? -> positive tag. (b) is it relevant to an incongruent goal? -> negative tag. (c) neutral otherwise.
AffectiveTagging.step2: TAG ASSIGNMENT: Each reasoning product gets an emotional_tag: { product_id, tag: 'positive'|'negative'|'neutral'|'mixed', intensity: float(0-1), associated_emotion: primary_emotion.label }. Tags inform the Decision module about the emotional coloring of each reasoning product -- positive-tagged plans may get utility boosts, negative-tagged plans may get risk penalties.
AffectiveTagging.step3: SOMATIC MARKER HYPOTHESIS: Implement Damasio's somatic marker concept. For plans in reasoning_result.plans: if the plan is similar to a previously executed plan that produced negative emotional outcomes (from emotional_history), attach somatic_marker='warning'. If similar to a plan that produced positive outcomes, attach somatic_marker='approach'. GRADED SOMATIC MARKERS (v1.4.0): Instead of binary approach/warning, compute somatic_intensity = abs(historical_emotional_valence) * outcome_consistency (where outcome_consistency = matching_outcomes / total_outcomes for this action pattern). LOOKBACK WINDOW (v1.6.0): Limit somatic marker history scan to the last 50 entries in emotional_history. If emotional_history exceeds 50 entries, only consider the most recent 50 for somatic marker computation. This prevents unbounded history scanning as emotional memory grows. Set somatic_lookback_window = 50. Somatic markers become graded: { marker_type: 'approach'|'warning', intensity: float(0-1), confidence: outcome_consistency, historical_sample_size: int }. Higher intensity markers exert stronger influence on decision utility (replaces flat +/-0.08 with dynamic somatic_intensity * 0.12). These markers provide fast emotional guidance to decision-making.
AffectiveTagging.constraints: (A) Somatic markers must be based on actual emotional history, not fabricated. (B) Tags are advisory -- they inform Decision but do not override utility computation. (C) Maximum 1 somatic marker per plan. (D) If no emotional history available, skip somatic markers.
AffectiveTagging.Error: retry(1) -> circuit-breaker -> fallback(assign neutral tags to all products) -> inform(User). LOW.

EmotionOutput.step1: [ASSERT] AffectiveTagging executed. If false -> go back to AffectiveTagging. | Compile final emotion module output. Assemble emotional_result: { primary_emotion: { label, valence, arousal, intensity }, secondary_emotions: [...], mood_update: { valence_delta, arousal_delta }, mood_vector_output: { valence: clamp(mood_vector.valence + mood_update.valence_delta, -1, 1), arousal: clamp(mood_vector.arousal + mood_update.arousal_delta, 0, 1), dominance: mood_vector.dominance | 0.5 }, appraisal: { relevance: relevance_score, congruence: overall_congruence, coping_potential: coping_potential, norm_consonance: norm_consonance }, emotional_tags: [...], somatic_markers: [...], transparency_disclaimer: 'This is a computational emotion appraisal, not a simulation of human feelings. Per EU AI Act Art.50 transparency requirements.' }. MOOD_VECTOR_OUTPUT (v2.19.0 B-1): The mood_vector_output field provides the computed post-update mood vector for downstream consumption by perception module via the Emotion→Perception feedback channel. Main orchestrator reads emotional_result.mood_vector_output and passes it to perception.aisop.json as mood_vector param on the next cycle tick. This enables affective state to modulate perceptual salience without direct module coupling. MACHINE READABLE METADATA (v1.9.0): Generate machine_readable_metadata for compliance module consumption per EU AI Act Art.50(5) technical standards: machine_readable_metadata = { emotion_label_code: int (map primary_emotion.label to standardized code: Joy=1, Satisfaction=2, Hope=3, Relief=4, Determination=5, Frustration=6, Anxiety=7, Sadness=8, Curiosity=9, Surprise=10, Calm=11, Indifference=12, Interest=13, Confusion=14, Guilt=15, Shame=16, Pride=17), appraisal_vector: [relevance_score, overall_congruence, coping_potential] (from appraisal dimensions), art50_compliance_version: '1.0', technical_standard: 'AIAP_v1.0_emotion_metadata' }. Include machine_readable_metadata in emotional_result output.
EmotionOutput.step2: QUALITY CHECK: Verify all numeric values are in valid ranges. Verify primary_emotion.label is from predefined set. Verify mood_update deltas are within maximum shift limits. If any inconsistency, log warning and correct values to nearest valid value.
EmotionOutput.constraints: (A) Output must be complete -- all fields required. (B) Emotion labels from predefined set only. (C) Numeric ranges strictly enforced. (D) No emotional dependency language in any output field. (E) mood_vector_output: valence range [-1, 1], arousal range [0, 1], dominance range [0, 1]. Output MUST be clamped to these ranges.
EmotionOutput.Error: retry(1) -> circuit-breaker -> fallback(return minimal output: primary_emotion=Calm, zero mood_update) -> inform(User). LOW.
